primary_source.title: Maintaining Queries under Updates Using Heavy-Light Partitioning of the Input Relations
primary_source.published_version: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data, volume 4, issue 2, May 2026
primary_source.identity_check: Title/authors/venue verified against author arXiv full text and Oxford publication listing; ACM full-text endpoint unavailable in prior scan, but this cycle used the author full-text preprint. Publication-version delta remains unaudited.

source_theorem.query_scope: Any fixed full conjunctive/join query in data complexity; free-variable CQ extension is described as a standard extension via free-connex hypertree decompositions, not the theorem's direct scope.
source_theorem.database_semantics: Relations map tuples to integer multiplicities over the Z ring. Support determines presence for set operations; output enumeration lists distinct tuples with multiplicities. Self-join atoms are handled as separate relation copies.
source_theorem.updates: Sequential single-tuple insertions and deletions, multiplicity changes +1/-1.
state: heavy/light value partitions per join variable
selected materialized view tree(s) for configurations
source_theorem.threshold: A query-level exponent epsilon in [0,1] is optimized once by minimizing maintenance width; the exponent stays fixed during the update sequence. The scale base M tracks database size.
source_theorem.heavy_light_membership: Global degree across all atoms containing a join variable; source relaxes boundary to light degree <= about 3/2 M^epsilon and heavy degree > about 1/2 M^epsilon to avoid oscillation.
source_theorem.mechanism: Delta-view trees, degree-configuration-dependent view selection, degree-constraint polymatroid/AGM LP bounds, maintenance-width optimization, minor and major rebalancing.

guarantee.space_bound: No separate asymptotic peak-space theorem for the entire materialized state is stated in Theorem 11; this audit makes no inferred portfolio-space claim.

rebalancing_audit.minor_rebalancing_cost: O(N^mw M^epsilon) per transition; Omega(M^epsilon) updates separate transitions, yielding amortized O(N^mw) per update.
rebalancing_audit.major_rebalancing_cost: Recompute partitions, fragments, and view trees when N leaves the M/4 <= N < M band; preprocessing-scale O(N^(1+mw)) work amortizes across Omega(N) updates to O(N^mw) per update.
rebalancing_audit.interpretation: The proposed broad dynamic-skew premise is already handled for membership/size drift. A narrower data-instance-dependent online epsilon policy is distinct but not shown to improve a defined guarantee.

formal_candidate_problem.input: Fixed query Q, initial multiset database D0, sequential single-tuple +/-1 update stream u1..uT, with state Dt and exact result Q(Dt).
formal_candidate_problem.policy_information: Online epsilon_t may use Q, current database statistics, and update history available before the decision; no future updates.
formal_candidate_problem.state: Selected epsilon, current partitions/fragments/views, active query version, migration/replay state.
formal_candidate_problem.invariant: At every committed update t, active materialized state enumerates exactly Q(Dt) with declared delay.
total_cost_components: dual maintenance or log replay during migration

benchmarks.fixed_initial_epsilon: online baseline; paper minimizes worst-case query exponent over all degree configurations
benchmarks.fixed_epsilon_with_size_scaling: already supported by M-based major rebalancing
benchmarks.best_fixed_epsilon_hindsight: offline comparator, not available to policy
benchmarks.offline_dynamic_epsilon_sequence: stronger oracle requiring explicit switching costs

prior_art.result: Generic heavy-light IVM for fixed join queries with per-configuration view trees, fixed query-optimal epsilon, exact output, constant delay, and amortized rebalancing.
prior_art.scope_boundary: Does not state online per-instance epsilon_t optimization with a migration-cost competitive bound.

prior_art.work: Kara et al., Maintaining Triangle Queries under Updates (IVM-epsilon), ICDT 2019/TODS 2020
prior_art.result: Threshold trade-offs in update time, space and enumeration delay, heavy-light partitioning and amortized rebalancing for triangle query; 2026 paper explicitly adapts its rebalancing technique.
prior_art.scope_boundary: Query-specific; confirms thresholding and rebalancing are established mechanisms.

prior_art.work: Kara et al., Conjunctive Queries with Free Access Patterns under Updates, LMCS 2025
prior_art.result: Fully dynamic CQ evaluation with access patterns and update/delay trade-offs.
prior_art.scope_boundary: Broader dynamic degree/partition context; no per-instance adaptive epsilon theorem authenticated here.

prior_art.work: Kara et al., F-IVM, VLDB Journal 2024
prior_art.result: Higher-order factorized view maintenance; materialization choices depend on static/updatable relations and update workload.
prior_art.scope_boundary: Update-workload-adaptive views are not the same as dynamic heavy-light exponent selection.

prior_art.work: Liang, Elmore, and Krishnan, Opportunistic View Materialization with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DQM), 2019
prior_art.result: Online RL creates/evicts opportunistic inner-join views under a storage cap using asynchronous paired counterfactual runtime experiments; tested across changing query patterns and skew in SparkSQL.
prior_art.scope_boundary: Prior art for dynamic view portfolio policies, but not exact tuple-level incremental maintenance: the paper recomputes affected views when base tables change. It reports experimental cumulative latency, not worst-case IVM update/delay guarantees.

prior_art.result: Delta and view-tree maintenance baselines for dynamic query execution.
prior_art.scope_boundary: Do not establish zero-cost threshold migration; included as relevant correctness/performance baselines.

prior_art.work: Materialized view selection and maintenance / view adaptation
prior_art.result: Prior view-selection and view-redefinition adaptation literature considers changing maintained view sets/workloads.
prior_art.scope_boundary: Different control variable and objective; cautions against treating migration or adaptive materialization as novel by itself.

adversarial_review.naive_rebuild_on_switch: For a policy alternating epsilon_A/epsilon_B states each one update, if each switch rebuilds affected views at preprocessing scale O(N^(1+mw)), transition cost can be Theta(T N^(1+mw)) versus fixed-threshold O(T N^mw) update maintenance while N remains in one band. This refutes that naïve implementation only, not all migration algorithms.
adversarial_review.naive_portfolio_problem: Several complete threshold states multiply view memory and update work; no equal-space guarantee was proved.

gate_results.gate2_uncovered_limitation: partial: instance-trajectory-dependent online epsilon selection is distinct, but no useful guarantee improvement established
gate_results.gate3_novel_mechanism: fail: portfolio, hysteresis, rebalancing, and migration are standard components; no new invariant/theorem
gate_results.gate6_precise_falsifiable_improvement_ta: fail: causal comparator and stream class remain unspecified

scientific_result.finding: Changing heavy/light membership and database size are already covered by the 2026 algorithm's minor/major rebalancing. Choosing epsilon from observed distribution is not shown to be novel or beneficial relative to the query-level minimax maintenance-width threshold.
scientific_result.smallest_unresolved_question: For a fixed query, can a causal epsilon_t policy lower total update-plus-transition work on a specified stream class versus the best fixed-epsilon scheme under equal peak space and exact constant-delay output?
scientific_result.valid_falsification: The naïve rebuild-on-every-switch portfolio implementation can lose Theta(N) versus fixed epsilon on an alternating stream, conditional on rebuild-scale transitions.
scientific_result.claim_scope: This falsifies the naïve implementation, not all online adaptive IVM. It does not establish the broader problem is closed.

future_evaluation.condition_to_proceed: First specify a migration-correct algorithm and theorem-level benefit over a causal/fixed threshold baseline.
